original_question: For n > 39, is it true that the number of conjugacy classes in the symmetric group Sn of degree n is never a divisor of the order of Sn? In other words, is it true that, for n > 39, the number p(n) of integer partitions of n is never a divisor of n!?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.89 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": the open problem asking whether, for every n > 39, the number of conjugacy classes of S_n never divides |S_n|, equivalently whether p(n) never divides n!. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s exact wording. It has the correct threshold n > 39, the correct object S_n, the precise divisibility question, and the paper’s own equivalent reformulation in terms of the partition number p(n). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: To make the question maximally stand-alone, state explicitly that n ranges over the positive integers, i.e. the claim is for every integer n > 39. The paper does not add further hypotheses beyond what your draft already includes. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
refined_question: For every integer n > 39, does the number k(S_n) of conjugacy classes of the symmetric group S_n fail to divide the group order |S_n| = n!? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for every integer n > 39, is the partition number p(n) not a divisor of n!? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
justification: This is exactly Problem 21.89, not a broader neighboring conjecture or theorem. In the paper, it appears as a standalone open problem and immediately includes the equivalent partition-theoretic restatement. Since no additional local assumptions or notation are supplied there, the sharp paper-faithful rewrite is simply to make the universal quantifier on n explicit while leaving the threshold 39 and the two equivalent formulations unchanged. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
